li.p: Explain why the homogeneous equation A\xvec = \zerovec is consistent no matter the matrix A.

Consider the matrix
A = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 3 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ -1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 2 \amp 1 \amp 1 \end{array}\right]
whose columns we denote by \vvec_1, \vvec_2, and \vvec_3. Describe the solution space of the homogeneous equation A\xvec = \zerovec using a parametric description, if appropriate.

Find a nonzero solution to the homogeneous equation and use it to find weights c_1, c_2, and c_3 such that
c_1\vvec_1 + c_2\vvec_2 + c_3\vvec_3 = \zerovec .
Use the equation you found in the previous part to write one of the vectors as a linear combination of the others.
Are the vectors \vvec_1, \vvec_2, and \vvec_3 linearly dependent or independent?
The vector \zerovec is always a solution.
We may rewrite this expression as \vvec_3=2\vvec_1-3\vvec_2, showing that \vvec_3 is a linear combination of \vvec_1 and \vvec_2.

The vectors \vvec_1, \vvec_2, and \vvec_3 are linearly dependent, and we know this in two ways. We have seen how to express one vector as a linear combination of the others. Also, we have seen that the associated matrix has a column without a pivot position.
